initialGeneration.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: original pixel-art mascot logo concept for SealCode, standalone transparent PNG.
Primary request: design from scratch a friendly SEAL PROGRAMMER actively typing code at a computer. Invent a fresh character and composition, not a variation of an existing mascot.
Subject and storytelling: a recognizable plump young seal, rounded head with no external ears, short whiskers, a tiny dark triangular nose, expressive attentive eyes, little tail flippers, and two natural front flippers resting on a laptop keyboard as it types. The seal sits on the left in a compact three-quarter view, focused on the open laptop on the right. Arrange the laptop in a coherent three-quarter angle so we can see both the keyboard under its flippers and part of the lit screen with a few tiny blue and pale code-like pixel lines and a small </> glyph. The seal's face remains visible, calm and slightly pleased. The body and laptop form one compact memorable silhouette. No headphones, clothing, desk, chair, mugs, props or extra objects; let the seal and the act of programming carry the idea.
Style/medium: expertly crafted 16-bit pixel-art mascot, designed as if on a low-resolution grid around 112 x 96 pixels and enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Distinct square pixels, consistent grid, crisp stepped contours, deliberate clusters. Minimalist enough for a website logo, with tasteful moderate detail. Restrained 12–16 color palette: pale silver-grey seal, cool slate-grey shaded areas, charcoal outlines and laptop, small blue screen accents. Friendly natural seal anatomy, flippers rather than human hands or paws.
Shading: directional upper-left light, 3–4 stepped shades on the rounded forehead and body, small crisp eye highlights, subtle pixel shadows where flippers meet the keyboard, clean highlights on the laptop rim. Pixel clusters rather than soft airbrush gradients; very little or no dithering. No fur texture or busy speckles.
Composition: single complete mascot illustration, compact horizontal near-square logo framing, comfortable narrow transparent margins, no cropped flippers or computer corners. Readable silhouette and facial expression at small sizes, particularly about 120px width.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha channel around the entire silhouette and in all interior empty gaps. Character and computer opaque. No ground plane or cast shadow outside the objects, no colored square, circle, badge, gradient backdrop, glow, halo or checkerboard baked into the image.
Text: only a few abstract code lines and a tiny </> on the laptop screen, no words, brand name, captions or watermark.
Avoid: photorealism, 3D rendering, smooth vector cartoon outlines, large smooth gradients, humanoid fingers, cat/dog ears, a walrus with tusks, multiple characters, presentation boards or multiple variations. Return one original finished transparent pixel-art logo.

refinement.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image: edit target, a new original pixel-art seal programmer logo.
Make exactly one local design correction to the LAPTOP LID: the visible panel at the right is the exterior BACK COVER of the laptop, so remove all the blue and white code-line UI markings from that panel. Replace them with ONE clean medium-size centered pale electric-blue pixel-art "</>" emblem. Treat the surface as an opaque charcoal laptop back with existing simple pixel shading, not a screen. Keep its existing shape, orientation, rim and hinge; the actual display faces the seal on the hidden inner side.
Preserve the seal character, pose, face, eyes, smile, whiskers, body, tail, flippers typing on the keyboard, all pixel shading, colors, outlines, keyboard perspective, composition, size and transparent margins unchanged. Preserve the pixel-art style and real alpha transparency in the whole background and internal gaps. Character and laptop remain opaque. Do not introduce text, floor, shadow, backdrop, glow, halos or new accessories.
Return the single corrected standalone transparent PNG logo.
